rule.resolves_from: The row's section_type when the census names it (a scalar row: extract.py:707 sets section_type to the census code S00..S32). Otherwise the leading code of the row's section_id (text before the first dot): the producer builds a chart row's id as '<census code>.chart.<slug of the section title>' at ycharts/extract/extract.py:772 ("%s.chart.%s" % (s["id"], _slug(s["title"])), where s["id"] is the census section id, extract.py:219-240 and 723-724), and the type token at :773; publication.py:71 sends the same type for a re-derived chart row with the section_id carried through unchanged (row["section_id"]). That leading code is looked up in the census's 33 names. The slug is not used.
rule.unresolvable: A row whose type and section_id prefix both miss the census prints UNNAMED_SECTION_TITLE = 'A section the census does not name', the one constant (vendorSectionNames.ts:70). Never the token, never the code.
rule.opal: unchanged: the Opal adapter does not call vendorCardTitle (iv-e-115 arm (e) passes unmodified).

chart_card.word_proposed: Chart from the source report; no figures read
chart_card.word_basis: What the producer says the row is: extract.py:738-744 and :782-785 ('identified source chart: <title>, page N. NO NUMERIC VALUE IS EMITTED -- the census declares zero field rows for this region'), value null, units 'chart'; certify.py:173-178 grades it PASS only when value is null and _emitted_values is 0 ('source-chart representation, 0 numeric values emitted for the region'); publication.py:61-63 ('a source representation, not numeric extraction or a claim to have detected chart pixels'). So the row says that a chart sits on that page of the source report and that nothing was read off it. The word says both halves in plain English and uses no vendor term.
chart_card.alternative_rejected: 'Chart image' / 'Chart': rejected because the card shows no picture, and the unit column already says 'chart'; the reader's actual question is why the Value is empty, which only the second half ('no figures read') answers.
chart_card.where_printed: As the card's Label cell (the Label column appears on a chart card because its Label differs from its title; a value card keeps IV-e-116's no-Label-column layout). The title above it is the section's census name, e.g. '5. Asset Allocation'.
chart_card.where_it_lives: census member row_type_words.source_chart_representation in docs/briefs/sources/YCHARTS_COMPARISON_REPORT_FIELD_SCRAPE_20260909.json; copied to VENDOR_ROW_TYPE_WORDS (vendorSectionNames.ts:65) and held equal by the IV-e-115 drift test arm (a).
